label: A necessary concrete power-holder, by Aristotelian modality and Pruss's possibility
meaning: Analyst reconstruction of Pruss's Aristotelian-modality argument with his own possibility premise. A concrete being is contingent at w, so not every actual contingent concretum is absent at w, while some accessible world lacks them all (P4-prime). Aristotelian grounding (P1-prime) gives a being y existing at w with a power for that absence; initiator presence (P2-prime) gives an accessible world v where it obtains and y exists; y is concrete (P3-prime). Were y absent at some world accessible from w, y would be a concrete being contingent at w, hence absent at v, where it exists. So, with excluded middle, y exists at every world accessible from w. No Euclidean premise: the holder's non-contingency is shown at w directly.

strong_version_needed.ee4ab504-c8fe-59bc-bc96-7cbeefed6410: The proof applies excluded middle to propositions outside LocalLogic's scope, e.g. `F.history.ontic.ExistsAt u y`. LocalLogic (ca432e24) decides only whether an actual bearer is identical with a GOD_4 candidate, and gives double-negation elimination for that candidate's esse–essence identity.
